scenario.description: A data engineering team is tasked with building a new real-time data ingestion pipeline for sensor data from IoT devices. The pipeline needs to process data at high velocity, ensuring data integrity and low latency, while also adhering to strict storage and processing cost limitations. The team consists of a Lead Data Engineer, a Data Architect, a Pipeline Developer, and a QA Engineer. The Lead Data Engineer oversees the project and orchestrates tasks. The Data Architect designs the overall system and ensures scalability. The Pipeline Developer implements the data flow components. The QA Engineer validates data quality and performance. A crucial constraint is that the average processing cost must not exceed $0.005 USD per GB, and the maximum end-to-end latency for any data point must be strictly less than 2.00 seconds. The team operates in a fully connected topology to facilitate rapid, iterative communication and immediate feedback, which is vital for balancing performance, cost, and latency in a real-time data environment. This medium structural-complexity task requires the team to consistently propagate these precise numerical constraints across 14 turns of interaction, ensuring they are reflected in the final pipeline design and implementation plan.
